sections.h2: Which Powell County offices deal with a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices in Stanton cover almost every question a Powell County owner has. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value, the sheriff takes the money, and the county clerk records liens and deeds. None of the three sets the rate. That is done by the fiscal court, the school board and the other taxing districts that appear on the bill.

Powell County, KY offices that touch a property tax account
OfficePhoneWhat it handles
Property Valuation Administrator(606) 663-4184Assessed value, exemptions, vehicle values
Sheriff(606) 663-2226Bills and payment through April 15
County Clerk(606) 663-6444Delinquent bills after April 15, deeds, lien records

The Powell County PVA works from 525 Washington Street in Stanton, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 277 (ZIP 40380) and a fax line at (606) 663-0947. The county site publishes these details on its PVA page. Call before driving over if you need a specific deputy, since the posted hours for the sheriff and the clerk differ from day to day.

sections.h2: How is a Powell County house valued for tax?
sections.html:
The PVA appraises every parcel at fair market value as it stood on January 1. The office says plainly that it does not decide how much tax you pay, because the bill is the assessed value multiplied by rates that other bodies vote on. Vehicles follow the same January 1 rule, using NADA guidelines, with adjustments allowed for high mileage or two written repair estimates from licensed body shops.

Kentucky lets an owner skip the annual listing if the parcel was described fully and correctly on last year's roll and nothing significant changed. A house bought during the previous year can carry the deed price as its listed value for the next January 1, as long as no changes affected what it is worth. That detail matters in Powell County, where a recent purchase price often becomes the starting point for the assessment.

Personal property such as business equipment must be listed with the PVA between January 1 and May 15. Anything not listed by May 15 counts as omitted, and the state may bill it later.

sections.h2: When must Powell County property tax be paid?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015, the full bill is due by December 31 of the assessment year, and the sheriff is the person who collects it. The statute sets the standard steps:

  • Paid in full by November 1: a 2 percent discount comes off the amount due.
  • November 2 through December 31: the face amount, with no discount or penalty.
  • January 1 through January 31: a 5 percent penalty on the unpaid tax.
  • After January 31: a 10 percent penalty, and the Department of Revenue notes that sheriffs add their own fee on top.

If bill mailing runs late, the Department of Revenue can substitute an alternative schedule. Tax then falls due two full months after mailing, the discount lasts one month, and each later stage also lasts one month. Because the choice varies by year, ask the Powell County Sheriff at (606) 663-2226 which calendar printed on your bill.

Unpaid bills go to the county clerk when the sheriff closes the books on April 15, and they become certificates of delinquency with a recorded lien.

sections.h2: What does a Powell County bill add up to?
sections.html:
For 2025 the state set its real property rate at 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents in 2024. On the $141,100 median value that Census QuickFacts reports for Powell County, the state's share alone comes to about $149.57. County, school and district rates ride on top of that, so the total depends on the address and the taxing districts that cover it.

An owner who qualifies for the homestead exemption pays on a smaller base. Taking $49,100 off the same $141,100 leaves $92,000, and the state share drops to roughly $97.52. Anyone who pays by November 1 also trims 2 percent from the final figure.

For a seller, the practical question is who covers the bill for the year of the sale. The owner on January 1 is the person the tax follows, so the purchase contract should say how the bill is split. Ask the sheriff for a payoff figure on the parcel before the closing date.

sections.h2: How can a Powell County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
The path starts with a conference with the PVA or a deputy, and nothing can be appealed without one. The tax roll opens for public inspection on the first Monday in May and stays open for thirteen days afterward, six days a week including Saturday. Notices of higher values must be sent to the owner under KRS 132.450.

  • At the conference, the PVA explains how the value was reached and keeps a written record of your claimed value and any offer.
  • The appeal goes to the local board of assessment appeals by filing at the county clerk's office, no later than the close of business the day after inspection ends.
  • The board meets 25 to 35 days after inspection and can sit up to five days.
  • You must bring evidence: land and building details, insurance policies, construction cost and sales listings. Without it the appeal is denied.

Anyone paid to speak for you must be on the statutory list, which includes attorneys, CPAs, licensed brokers and licensed or certified appraisers, and must carry written authorization. If bills go out before the appeal ends and the final value is higher than your claim, you receive a supplemental bill for the difference.

sections.h2: Who can get the homestead exemption in Powell County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can claim it on the home they live in. The Department of Revenue set the deduction at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Apply at the PVA office on Washington Street, and bring proof of age such as a birth certificate, driver's license or passport.

A married couple gets one exemption, and either spouse reaching 65 satisfies the age test. Once approved, an age-based claim carries forward while the same owner lives in the house. Disability claims must be renewed each year unless the owner is a service-connected disabled veteran or has been found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

The exemption belongs to the owner and not to the property. A buyer who qualifies has to file again after the sale, and a seller who moves should tell the PVA so the old account is cleaned up.

sections.h2: What happens when a Powell County tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Selling the house does not erase the debt. KRS 134.015 treats the tax as a personal debt of the person who owned the property on the assessment date, and a lien from KRS 134.420 stays on the parcel for eleven years regardless of who holds title. A title search at the county clerk will turn it up.

After April 15 the clerk adds interest of 1 percent per month. The state's worked example shows a $1,000 bill becoming $1,254 at transfer, once a 10 percent penalty, a sheriff add-on fee and a commission are counted. Later come clerk and county attorney commissions, postage and a $10 lien fee, which pushed the example to $1,387.79 within five business days and $1,611.30 after the first attorney notice.

Tax sales must fall between 90 and 135 days after the transfer, and a buyer at the sale gains a lien that can carry its own interest and costs. Paying the sheriff before April 15 avoids all of this.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Powell County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Powell County was formed in 1852 from parts of Clark, Estill and Montgomery counties, and Stanton is the seat. Clay City is the only other incorporated town. Land area is about 179 square miles in the foothills of the Appalachians, with elevations from 580 to 1,440 feet, and part of the Daniel Boone National Forest lies inside the line. Natural Bridge State Resort Park and the Red River Gorge Geologic Area draw outdoor visitors, and the county says two major interstate highways are only minutes away.

Census QuickFacts gives this picture of the housing market:

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 12,812, down 2.4 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 68.2 percent, across 4,790 households of 2.65 people.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $141,100; median gross rent: $747.
  • Median household income: $40,309, with 20.8 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Building permits in 2025: 5, so most sales are existing houses.

Neighbors are Montgomery, Menifee, Wolfe, Lee, Estill and Clark counties. Commutes average 26.6 minutes, and 79.7 percent of households have broadband. A house with deferred repairs or back taxes can be sold as-is for cash, with the tax settled out of the proceeds.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Powell County?
faqs.a: The Powell County Sheriff, at (606) 663-2226. The PVA at (606) 663-4184 sets values only and does not take payments or set rates.

faqs.q: What is the early payment discount for Powell County property tax?
faqs.a: Two percent, for bills paid in full by November 1 under the regular schedule in KRS 134.015. If the state moves to an alternative schedule, the discount lasts one month from the mailing date instead.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead exemption in Powell County?
faqs.a: $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It comes off the assessed value of an owner's home if the owner is 65 or older or totally disabled, and the application goes to the PVA.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Powell County assessment without meeting the PVA first?
faqs.a: No. A conference with the PVA or a deputy has to happen before an appeal can be filed. The appeal then goes to the county clerk by the close of business on the day after the inspection period ends.

faqs.q: Do Powell County taxes stay with a house after I sell it?
faqs.a: Unpaid ones do. The tax is the owner's personal debt from the January 1 assessment date, and a lien on the parcel lasts up to eleven years, so the contract and the closing statement should settle the current year.
